name: Van Hilleary
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Former four-term U.S. Rep and 2002 GOP gubernatorial nominee. Was Rose's chief of staff, bringing D.C. experience to the open primary.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Congressional record (1995–2003) shows support for school choice via vouchers and accountability testing, with no stated position on early childhood or pre-K in the current 2026 campaign.
early_childhood_ed.details: During his four terms in Congress, Hilleary voted YES on the No Child Left Behind Act of 2001. He also voted YES on vouchers for private and parochial schools (1997) and DC school vouchers (1998), reflecting a school-choice philosophy. His 2026 campaign website emphasizes 'Veteran. Conservative. Fighter.' branding aligned with Public Safety, Affordability, Freedom, and Energy priorities — with no specific platform on early childhood or pre-K education.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found on child hunger in the 2026 campaign; 1994 Contract with America included welfare cuts that limited AFDC benefits.
child_hunger.details: Hilleary signed the Contract with America in 1994 pledging to pass the Personal Responsibility Act, which aimed to cut welfare spending, prohibit welfare to minor mothers, and deny increased AFDC for additional children while on welfare. No specific votes on child nutrition programs (school lunch, WIC, food stamps) or statements on child hunger have been identified for his congressional tenure or 2026 campaign.

parental_support.summary: Supported the child tax credit expansion and family tax relief in Congress; signed Contract with America's Families Reinforcement Act for child support enforcement and parental rights.
parental_support.details: In 2001, Hilleary voted YES on reducing the marriage tax penalty by $399 billion over 10 years (HR 6), which doubled the child tax credit for married couples. He signed the Contract with America's Families Reinforcement Act in 1994. His 2026 campaign platform has not published specific positions on paid family leave, modern childcare costs, or current child tax credit policy.

name: Johnny Garrett
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: State legislator from Goodlettsville. First to file petitions; raised $1.1M with $1M+ cash on hand. Strong grassroots support.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Sponsored HB 1175 in the Tennessee legislature, related to childcare and school property leasing; supports the Education Freedom Scholarship for school choice but has not stated a position on federal pre-K or Head Start.
early_childhood_ed.details: As TN House Majority Whip, Garrett sponsored HB 1175, which relates to childcare providers leasing school district property — signaling engagement with childcare access at the state level. He is also a proponent of the Education Freedom Scholarship program, Tennessee's school choice voucher initiative. His congressional campaign platform lists America First priorities — border security, economy, taxes, Second Amendment, law enforcement, pro-life, and AI innovation — with no mention of early childhood education or pre-K at the federal level.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found on child hunger, school meals, or child nutrition programs.
child_hunger.details: Garrett's campaign platform makes no mention of child nutrition, SNAP, school lunch, or food assistance programs. His issue page focuses on immigration, economy, taxes, Second Amendment, Israel, law enforcement, pro-life stance, China, farmers, and AI — with no reference to child hunger or food security.

parental_support.summary: Identifies as a 'conservative family values' candidate and 'husband and father of three' but has not published specific positions on paid family leave, child tax credits, or childcare costs.
parental_support.details: Garrett's campaign centers on 'standing up for conservative family values' and explicitly lists 'Keeping Men Out Of Women's Sports' and 'Protecting The Sanctity Of Life' as parental-rights-adjacent issues. However, the campaign has published no specific policy positions on paid family leave, child tax credits, childcare affordability, or related parental support programs.

name: Dale Braden
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Republican primary candidate. Campaign suspended — confirmed by Tennessee Conservative News; campaign website is offline.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position found on early childhood education; campaign website lists no education policy. Campaign suspended.
early_childhood_ed.details: Braden's campaign website identified him as a 'conservative candidate' and 'political outsider' running on border security, lower inflation, protecting Social Security and Medicare, strengthening the military, and opposing the 'radical left's agenda.' Education policy, including early childhood education or pre-K, was not mentioned. His campaign has since been suspended, per Tennessee Conservative News, and the campaign website is offline.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found on child hunger or food assistance programs. Campaign suspended.
child_hunger.details: Braden's campaign platform did not address child nutrition, SNAP, WIC, or school meal programs. His stated priorities were immigration/border security, inflation, Social Security/Medicare, military, and opposing the progressive agenda. Campaign subsequently suspended.

parental_support.summary: No public position found on paid family leave, child tax credit, or childcare costs. Campaign suspended.
parental_support.details: Braden's campaign rhetoric referenced protecting against 'the radical left's agenda' and his opposition to transgender athletes in women's sports, sometimes framed in parental-rights terms. No explicit positions on paid family leave, child tax credits, childcare subsidies, or parental rights in education were identified before his campaign was suspended.

name: Mike Croley
primary_label: Democratic Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Democratic candidate facing a steep climb in this strongly Republican district.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No explicit pre-K or childcare investment positions found on the current croleyforcongress.com (crawled June 2026). His site covers healthcare, affordability, and democracy themes. Prior profile entries on these positions could not be confirmed from current site content.
early_childhood_ed.details: The campaign homepage and blog posts through May 2026 cover healthcare, marijuana legalization, gun rights, public lands, gerrymandering, and DOGE cuts. No early childhood education, pre-K, or childcare workforce content found in crawled pages. His 'AAA Blueprint' framework references 'accessibility' broadly.

child_hunger.summary: Croley's campaign homepage explicitly references cuts to SNAP and WIC as leaving families hungry — the most specific food security statement found in his profile. He has spoken against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's Medicaid/TennCare cuts as a healthcare crisis for Tennessee families.
child_hunger.details: The croleyforcongress.com homepage (last updated June 5, 2026) states: 'I've heard from parents who've had to dig into their savings because cuts to SNAP and WIC threaten to leave their families hungry.' A April 2026 blog post ('The Affordability Crisis Is a Healthcare Crisis') criticizes the OBBB for gutting Medicaid: 'The OBBB Act also gutted Medicaid, making it harder to apply for or qualify for benefits. Roughly $7 billion has been cut from TennCare, and we project that 45,000 to 75,000 Tennesseans will lose their coverage entirely.' School meal programs are not mentioned directly.

parental_support.summary: No explicit paid family leave or childcare affordability positions found on the current croleyforcongress.com (crawled June 2026). Prior profile entries on these positions could not be confirmed from current site content.
parental_support.details: Campaign website and blog posts do not address paid family leave, childcare affordability as a named commitment, or CTC expansion. Affordability is discussed in terms of healthcare and food costs.

name: Matt Van Epps
bio: Won the December 2025 special election after Mark Green's resignation. West Point graduate, combat veteran, and former state commissioner.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No public position found on early childhood education or pre-K.
early_childhood_ed.details: Van Epps's campaign issues page and his official House education page contain no specific language on early childhood education, Head Start, or pre-K programs. His platform focuses on cutting federal spending, supporting parental rights by opposing gender-affirming care for minors, and keeping Washington's 'radical agenda' out of schools. Van Epps took office December 4, 2025, and has not yet produced a federal legislative record on this issue.

child_hunger.summary: Van Epps supports the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut $186 billion from SNAP nationally. Tennessee SNAP enrollment dropped from ~696,000 (July 2025) to ~597,890 (May 2026) — roughly 100,000 Tennesseans lost food aid. Children enrolled in SNAP are automatically certified for free school meals, meaning SNAP losses also threaten school meal access. No Van Epps statement opposing or qualifying these cuts was found.
child_hunger.details: Van Epps's Club for Growth profile (October 2025) confirms he 'supports the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, tax cuts, and Medicaid reforms.' The OBBB, signed July 2025, cut $186 billion from SNAP and expanded work requirements. Tennessee Lookout (June 16, 2026) reported enrollment dropped from 696,000 to 597,890 between July 2025 and May 2026. Children enrolled in SNAP are automatically certified for free school meals (per Anderson, TCCY, cited in the Lookout report), so SNAP losses can directly affect school meal access. His mattfortn.com issues page (Economy, Veterans, Borders, Farmers, America First, Women's Sports) contains no child hunger or SNAP content. House.gov press releases (Feb–Mar 2026) focus on Gold Star families, terrorism, and district offices.

parental_support.summary: Has not stated positions on paid family leave, child tax credit, or subsidized childcare; opposes gender-affirming care for minors; affiliated with the Republican Study Committee (February 2026).
parental_support.details: The campaign platform explicitly opposes government-funded gender surgeries for minors and describes this as defending 'Tennessee families.' Van Epps supports protecting life from conception. He joined the Republican Study Committee in February 2026, a caucus that has historically opposed expansions of federal family benefit programs. No stated position on the Child Tax Credit was found, though as a freshman Republican he would likely support TCJA-style extensions.

name: David Kustoff
bio: Five-term incumbent attorney. Unopposed in Republican primary; $2.8M cash on hand.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No explicit early childhood education platform; voted against the American Rescue Plan, which funded Head Start and childcare stabilization.
early_childhood_ed.details: Kustoff's official issues page does not include a dedicated early childhood or pre-K category. He voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, which included $39 billion for childcare stabilization and expanded Head Start funding. He supported the 2018 Farm Bill, which reauthorized child nutrition programs. As a member of the Tennessee Higher Education Commission before his congressional service, he oversaw Tennessee Promise community college scholarships.

child_hunger.summary: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill which cuts $267 billion from SNAP, voted against SNAP expansions in the American Rescue Plan, and publicly defended the SNAP cuts in a September 2025 op-ed.
child_hunger.details: Kustoff voted NAY on the American Rescue Plan (2021), which included SNAP expansions, Pandemic EBT, WIC improvements, and child nutrition enhancements. He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025), which the CBO estimated would cut $267 billion from SNAP and impose new work requirements on recipients aged 55–64. In a September 22, 2025 op-ed in The Hill, Kustoff defended the OBBB's SNAP provisions, arguing the cuts would promote self-sufficiency and reduce waste in the program.

parental_support.summary: Supports an enhanced and permanent Child Tax Credit through the One Big Beautiful Bill; co-sponsored the bipartisan Save Struggling Hospitals Act (April 2026); holds an A+ pro-life rating (January 2026).
parental_support.details: Kustoff championed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as a Ways and Means Committee member, which includes an enhanced and permanent Child Tax Credit building on the 2017 TCJA's doubled CTC. He wrote in a June 2025 op-ed that the bill 'boosts the doubled child tax credit.' However, he voted NAY on the 2021 American Rescue Plan, which made the CTC fully refundable. In April 2026, he co-sponsored the bipartisan Save Struggling Hospitals Act with Rep. Terri Sewell (D-AL), addressing rural hospital access — a measure affecting family healthcare access. He holds an A+ pro-life rating as of January 2026.

early_childhood_ed.details: Dewey Bryan is listed as a Democratic primary candidate for TN-8 on Ballotpedia and Tennessee Secretary of State filings, but no campaign website, social media presence, or policy platform was discoverable as of April 2026. Ballotpedia lists him with a placeholder and no biography or issues.

child_hunger.details: No campaign website, press releases, or news coverage detailing Bryan's position on SNAP, school meals, WIC, or childhood food insecurity was found.

parental_support.details: No statements on paid family leave, the Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, or parental rights were found for Dewey Bryan. His candidacy is confirmed through official Tennessee election filings, but no public platform or media coverage of his policy positions was located.

name: Leonard Perkins
bio: Democratic primary candidate. Pastor and substance abuse counselor with 23 years of community service.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No early childhood education, pre-K, or childcare investment positions found on the current perkinstocongress.com (crawled June 17, 2026). The site's stated priorities are Veterans' Rights, Women's Rights, and Labor Rights.
early_childhood_ed.details: perkinstocongress.com (home and About pages, crawled June 17, 2026) lists top priorities as: 'Voting rights, Women's Rights, Organized Labor, Veterans/Survivors Benefits, Student Debt, Small Businesses, Our Democracy.' No childcare, pre-K, early childhood, or education content is present. The /issues page returns 404. Prior profile entries on these positions could not be confirmed from current site content.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific public position on early childhood education found for her TN-8 congressional campaign.
early_childhood_ed.details: Moses's published seven-point platform focuses on criminal justice reform, universal healthcare, food security, community health, environmental sustainability, youth violence prevention, and reparations. Youth-related planks include mentorship and leadership programs and investment in mental health services, but no explicit stance on pre-K, Head Start, childcare subsidies, or early learning programs.

child_hunger.details: Her platform calls for expanding farmers' markets in underserved areas to create direct farm-to-consumer channels, and for community education programs teaching people to grow their own food. She frames food security as central to community health. No explicit position on SNAP, WIC, school meal programs, or Summer EBT was found.

early_childhood_ed.details: Taylor's Ballotpedia 2026 Candidate Connection survey identifies education as one of his key passions alongside cost of living and agriculture. name: Steve Cohen
bio: Memphis-area Democratic congressman serving since 2007. Announced May 15, 2026 he would not seek reelection after redistricting dismantled TN-9, but left the door open if legal challenges succeed. cohenforcongress.com remains active and he cosponsored the Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026 (H.R. 8798) in May 2026.
status_line: Conditional retirement announced May 15, 2026 · Active if redistricting lawsuit succeeds

early_childhood_ed.summary: Has been a consistent and long-standing champion of Head Start, Early Head Start, and pre-K programs, securing tens of millions of dollars in federal grants for Memphis-area providers — including a $7.4 million Head Start grant to Shelby County Board of Education in April 2025.
early_childhood_ed.details: Cohen has repeatedly announced and championed Head Start grants for Memphis-area providers: $7.4 million to Shelby County Board of Education (April 2025), $35.5 million for Porter-Leath (July 2025), $2.6 million (December 2024), and $1.1 million for Early Head Start at Children's Bureau (2018). He strongly opposed GOP efforts in 2015 to eliminate the Preschool Development Grant program, which he said would have cut $7 million from Shelby County Schools and denied preschool to nearly 7,500 low- and moderate-income Tennessee children. He has also cited the Gospel of Matthew on the House floor in arguments for investing in poor children, and championed the Fix America's Schools Today (FAST) Act.

child_hunger.summary: Cohen cosponsored H.R. 8798 (Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026, May 13, 2026), which would provide free breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a snack to every student nationwide, expand SUN Bucks (Summer EBT) to all children regardless of income, and eliminate school meal debt. He has a long record opposing SNAP cuts and calling the OBBB 'cruel and immoral.'
child_hunger.details: Cohen is named as a cosponsor of H.R. 8798, introduced May 13, 2026 by Rep. Gwen Moore. The bill: (1) provides universal free school meals regardless of family income; (2) expands SUN Bucks/Summer EBT to all communities; (3) eliminates school meal debt collection; (4) strengthens the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) to allow three meals and a snack per day and equalizes reimbursement rates for childcare providers. The bill directly responds to the OBBB's $186B SNAP cuts. Tennessee has lost ~100,000 SNAP recipients since July 2025. Cohen has previously called the OBBB 'cruel and immoral' regarding its SNAP provisions.

parental_support.summary: Persistent cosponsor of the FAMILY Act for national paid family leave; voted in February 2024 to expand the Child Tax Credit for 79,000 Memphis children; has supported childcare and parental support broadly.
parental_support.details: Cohen has continuously cosponsored the Family and Medical Insurance Leave (FAMILY) Act, which would create a permanent, national paid family and medical leave program. In February 2024 he voted for H.R. 7024, a bipartisan bill expanding the Child Tax Credit's refundability, which he estimated would benefit 79,000 children in Memphis and TN-9. He stated: 'I voted to pass a tax package that would expand the Child Tax Credit for 79,000 kids in Memphis and TN-9, lifting many of them out of poverty.' He also voted against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, calling it 'likely the worst bill ever presented' for Memphis families.

name: Justin J. Pearson
bio: Progressive challenger known for the Byhalia Pipeline fight and the 2023 'Tennessee Three' gun-protest expulsion. Pledging no corporate PAC money; raised $374K in Q1 2026 alone, narrowly outraising Cohen that quarter. Justice Democrats endorsed; pledged $1M through Leaders We Deserve. ⚠ The new map signed May 7 dismantles the Memphis-based TN-9; Pearson's brother KeShaun was arrested protesting at the Capitol. All candidates must refile by May 15; Pearson's campaign path in the redrawn district is unclear pending legal challenges.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pearson lists 'Educational Equity & Funding Our Schools' as a named campaign issue, but his current website does not contain explicit universal pre-K or childcare investment language. He has spoken about the importance of 'a good school that they can send their kids to' as part of his anti-poverty platform.
early_childhood_ed.details: votejustinj.com/issues (crawled June 17, 2026) lists 'Educational Equity & Funding Our Schools' among his ten issue areas and states he will fight to 'invest in quality educational opportunities for our students.' In a May 29, 2026 American Prospect Q&A, he stated 'most people want...a good school that they can send their kids to.' No explicit universal pre-K, childcare investment, or childcare workforce language found on the current campaign site. His TN state legislative record includes education equity work, but federal pre-K commitments are not articulated on the current site.

child_hunger.summary: Pearson's platform explicitly names child poverty as a central crisis ('33% of our children live below the poverty line'), commits to doubling the Earned Income Tax Credit to lift children out of poverty, and invokes 'food justice' as a moral and legislative responsibility. No explicit SNAP-specific or Summer EBT positions found on the current site.
child_hunger.details: votejustinj.com/issues states: '33% of our children live below the poverty line. That has been worsening for the last two decades.' Under End Poverty & the Affordability Crisis, he pledges to: 'double the Earned Income Tax Credit which would lift half of children in the country out of poverty'; 'cut taxes on working class people and end the grocery tax.' His Affordable Housing section invokes Matthew 25: 'we have moral and legislative responsibility to ensure housing and food justice for all.' At a June 15, 2026 forum he referenced 'Trump was spending billions of dollars on war but was unable to help those in need.' No explicit SNAP defense, SUN Bucks, or school meal language found in May–June 2026 content.

parental_support.summary: Pearson's current platform focuses on poverty reduction through EITC doubling, minimum wage increases, and Guaranteed Basic Income programs. No explicit paid family leave, childcare affordability, or child tax credit expansion language found on the current campaign website.
parental_support.details: votejustinj.com/issues 'End Poverty' section pledges: 'Writing legislation to increase the minimum wage'; doubling the EITC; Guaranteed Basic Income programs for people experiencing poverty; and tax cuts on working class people. No paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or CTC expansion language appears on the current site.

name: Charlotte Bergmann
bio: Republican nominee in a D+35 district.

early_childhood_ed.details: The electbergmann.com home page (crawled June 17, 2026) lists four pillars: Crime & Safety; Veterans; Economy & Jobs; and School Choice ('Empowering parents and protecting children's futures'). The /issues page returns 404. School choice framing suggests parental empowerment in K-12 rather than government-directed early childhood programs.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public position found on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, or food assistance programs.
child_hunger.details: Bergmann's campaign platform lists 'Protect the Children and Babies' as a stated priority alongside jobs, veterans, and law and justice, but no details on child nutrition, school lunch programs, SNAP, WIC, or Summer EBT are provided in her publicly available campaign materials.

parental_support.summary: No specific public position found on paid family leave, the Child Tax Credit, childcare costs, or parental rights beyond a general commitment to protecting children.

She identifies as an America First conservative and supports the elimination of what she characterizes as 'dependency' on government programs.
